page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-64 is a compute-focused instance powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The machine configuration provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance provision includes 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio tailored for CPU-intensive processing rather than data footprint caching. No local storage is attached by default, requiring reliance on external networked volumes, and the configuration includes zero GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong raw computation and algorithmic capabilities. The instance records strong tier outcomes in stress-ng multi-core testing at 86,418.33 and PassMark CPU score at 62,086.52, supported by strong performance in encryption (68,639.91) and physics computations (7,916.63). Geekbench execution registers solid ray tracing at 63,384.0 and image processing at 14,310.0. In contrast, workloads sensitive to large memory footprints or broader memory bandwidth exhibit moderate throughput, with uncached read transfers measuring 132.04 GB/sec and uncached writes at 59.49 GB/sec.

The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-effective resource profile for parallel computation where large memory overheads would introduce unutilized capacity. Workloads requiring dense compute capacity per gigabyte of memory benefit most from this layout. It is well matched for batch compute pipelines, parallel compilation, media transcoding, scientific ray tracing, and compute-heavy microservices.
